title: Cyclists in Japan Receive 16,000 'Blue Tickets' in 6 Months
paragraphs: Police in Japan have recorded nearly 16,000 bicycle traffic violations since April, according to data from the country's National Police Agency (NPA).
On April 1 of this year, the NPA started using a new "blue ticket" system, which lets police quickly fine cyclists for breaking traffic rules.

In the system's first six months, using a smartphone while riding was the most common violation, making up 43% of all tickets. Those caught riding while using a phone receive a fine of 12,000 yen, or about $76.

The second most common violation was failing to stop when required, followed by riding through a red light. Other common violations included entering a railroad crossing when the gate was down, and riding on the wrong side of the road.
These violations all carry fines of between 3,000 yen and 7,000 yen — or between about $19 and $44.
The rules must be followed by all cyclists aged 16 and over.
Tokyo had the highest number of tickets, with nearly 3,000, followed by Osaka with close to 2,900. Saitama recorded almost 1,900 violations, while Aichi had over 1,700.

The NPA also said that bicycle accidents decreased by about 9% between April and September compared with the same time last year. However, it said it's not clear if this is because of the new ticket system.
